chunks: O wonder! And why should I not wonder at the error of these groups, given the difference in their proofs within their religion!
They do not follow the trace of a Prophet, nor do they imitate the action of a Vicegerent, nor do they believe in the unseen, nor do they refrain from fault.
They act amidst doubts, and they walk in passions,
Good is what they recognize, and evil is what they reject,
Their refuge in difficulties is themselves, and their reliance in ambiguous matters is on their own opinions,
As if every one of them is the Imam of himself, who has taken from it what he sees as reliable proofs and firm reasons.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the error of sectarian groups in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the early sectarian groups for abandoning the clear authority of the Prophet and the Vicegerent (Imam Ali) in favor of subjective reasoning (ra'y) and personal desires. This passage highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the necessity of following the Infallible Imams to avoid the ambiguity of individual interpretation, contrasting divine guidance with human-centric religiosity.
